Then the henselizations $S^h$, $T^h$ of $S$, $T$ along $I$, $J$ fit into a Milnor square \[ \xymatrix{ S^h \ar[d] \ar[r] & T^h \ar[d] \\ S' \ar[r] & T' }.\] Furthermore, $T^h \simeq S^h \otimes_S T$.
nodes.statement_short: Henselization preserves Milnor squares and $T^h \simeq S^h \otimes_S T$.
assumptions: Consider a Milnor square as in \eqref{milnsquare} with respect to the ideals $I \subset S$, $J \subset T$.
conclusions: Then the henselizations $S^h$, $T^h$ of $S$, $T$ along $I$, $J$ fit into a Milnor square
Furthermore, $T^h \simeq S^h \otimes_S T$.

nodes.name: Proof that henselization preserves Milnor squares
nodes.statement: Since $S^h$ is flat over $S$, we can base-change \eqref{milnsquare} along $S \to S^h$ to obtain a new Milnor square \[ \xymatrix{ S^h \ar[d] \ar[r] & T \otimes_S S^h \ar[d] \\ S' \otimes_S S^h \ar[r] & T' \otimes_S S^h }. \] Note that $S' \otimes_S S^h \simeq S'$ by the properties of the henselization, and similarly for $T$. Therefore the bottom arrow can be rewritten as $S' \to T'$. Since this is a Milnor square and the left vertical arrow is a henselian pair, so is the right vertical arrow thanks to Proposition~\ref{checkhensnonunital}. We have a factorization $T \to T \otimes_S S^h \to T'$ as the composite of an ind-\'etale map and a map having the right lifting property with respect to \'etale maps. Thus, the result follows in view of Remark~\ref{hensfact}.
nodes.statement_short: Base-change along the flat map $S \to S^h$, then recognize the result as a henselization via the ind-\'etale factorization criterion.

nodes.name: Henselization of a nonunital ring is independent of the base ring
nodes.statement: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair and let $(S^h, I^h)$ be its henselization. Let $R$ be any ring mapping to $S$. Then $I^h$ is the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\nur$. In particular, the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\nur$ does not depend on the base ring $R$.
assumptions: Let $(S, I)$ be a pair and let $(S^h, I^h)$ be its henselization.
Let $R$ be any ring mapping to $S$.
conclusions: Then $I^h$ is the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\nur$.
In particular, the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\nur$ does not depend on the base ring $R$.

nodes.name: Proof of base-independence of the nonunital henselization
nodes.statement: To distinguish the possible henselizations which a priori might not coincide, we temporarily write $I^{nuh}$ to denote the henselization of $I$ as an object of $\nur$. The equivalence between $\nur$ and augmented $R$-algebras easily implies that $(R\ltimes I^{nuh},I^{nuh})$ is the henselization of the pair $(R \ltimes I, I)$. Applying Proposition~\ref{milnsquarehens} to the Milnor square \[ \xymatrix{ R\ltimes I \ar[d] \ar[r] & S \ar[d] \\ R \ar[r] & S/I }\] then reveals that the square \[ \xymatrix{ R\ltimes I^{nuh} \ar[d] \ar[r] & S^h \ar[d] \\ R \ar[r] & S^h/I^h }\] is also Milnor, i.e., that $I^{nuh}\isoto I^h$, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Milnor-square henselization lemma to the square $(R\ltimes I \to S; R \to S/I)$.

nodes.name: Free henselian nonunital $\mathbb{Q}$-algebras as colimits of $[N]$
nodes.statement: Let $n > 0$. The filtered colimit of the endomorphisms $[N]$ on $\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$, indexed over natural numbers $N$ ordered by divisibility, is $\mathbb{Q}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{Q}\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}^+$ is the filtered colimit of the multiplication-by-$N$ endomorphisms of $\mathbb{Z}\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}^+$.
assumptions: Let $n > 0$.
conclusions: The filtered colimit of the endomorphisms $[N]$ on $\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$, indexed over natural numbers $N$ ordered by divisibility, is $\mathbb{Q}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$.

nodes.name: Proof that the colimit of $[N]$ is the rational free henselian algebra
nodes.statement: Henselization commutes with filtered colimits, and the filtered colimit of the analogous maps $[N]: \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+$ is given by $\mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_n]^+$. We now use Corollary \ref{corollary_hens_ind_of_base} that henselization does not depend on the base ring.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to polynomial algebras and use that henselization commutes with filtered colimits and is base-independent.

nodes.name: finitely generated functor
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category and $F: \mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ a functor. We say that $F$ is \emph{finitely generated} if there exist finitely many objects $X_1, \dots, X_n \in \mathcal{C}$ and a surjection of functors \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{i=1}^t \mathbb{Z}[\hom_{\mathcal{C}}(X_i, \cdot)] \twoheadrightarrow F. \end{equation}
differentia: there exist finitely many objects $X_1, \dots, X_n \in \mathcal{C}$ and a surjection of functors $\bigoplus_{i=1}^t \mathbb{Z}[\hom_{\mathcal{C}}(X_i, \cdot)] \twoheadrightarrow F$

nodes.name: Surjection presenting a finitely generated functor
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{i=1}^t \mathbb{Z}[\hom_{\mathcal{C}}(X_i, \cdot)] \twoheadrightarrow F. \end{equation}

nodes.name: perfect and pseudocoherent functors
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category and $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ a functor. \begin{enumerate} \item We say that $F$ is \emph{perfect} if $F$ belongs to the thick subcategory of $\fun(\mathcal C,\Sp)$ generated by the functors $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(C, \cdot)$ for $C \in \mathcal{C}$ (or equivalently is a compact object of $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$, by a thick subcategory argument). \item We say that $F$ is \emph{pseudocoherent} if, for each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, there exists a perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to F$ such that $\tau_{\le n}F'(C)\to\tau_{\le n}F(C)$ is an equivalence for all $C\in \mathcal C$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Perfect = compact in $\fun(\mathcal{C},\Sp)$; pseudocoherent = approximable by perfect functors in every finite range.
differentia: for each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, there exists a perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to F$ such that $\tau_{\le n}F'(C)\to\tau_{\le n}F(C)$ is an equivalence for all $C\in \mathcal C$

nodes.name: Equivalent characterizations of pseudocoherence
nodes.statement: Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$. The following conditions on a functor $F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq d}) \subset \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $F$ is pseudocoherent. \item For each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, the functor $\tau_{\leq n} F$ is a compact object of the $\infty$-category $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$. \item There exists a sequence $G_{d-1} = 0 \to G_d \to G_{d+1} \to G_{d+2} \to \dots $ such that $G_i/G_{i-1}$ is a finite direct sum of functors of the form $\Sigma^i \Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(C, \cdot)$ for $C \in \mathcal{C}$ and such that $\varinjlim_i G_i \simeq F$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Pseudocoherence equals truncated compactness equals admitting a filtration by finite sums of shifted corepresentables.
assumptions: Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$.
a functor $F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq d}) \subset \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$
conclusions: $F$ is pseudocoherent.
For each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, the functor $\tau_{\leq n} F$ is a compact object of the $\infty$-category $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$.

There exists a sequence $G_{d-1} = 0 \to G_d \to G_{d+1} \to G_{d+2} \to \dots $ such that $G_i/G_{i-1}$ is a finite direct sum of functors of the form $\Sigma^i \Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(C, \cdot)$ for $C \in \mathcal{C}$ and such that $\varinjlim_i G_i \simeq F$.

nodes.name: Proof of the equivalent characterizations of pseudocoherence
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we can assume $d =0 $ by shifting. For (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2), suppose that $F\in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ (we do not need $F$ connective) is pseudocoherent and let $n\in\mathbb Z$. Then by definition there is a perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to F$ inducing an equivalence $\tau_{\leq n} F' \simeq \tau_{\leq n} F$. Since $\tau_{\leq n}: \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp) \to \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ preserves compact objects (as its right adjoint preserves filtered colimits), it follows that $\tau_{\leq n} F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ is compact. For (2) $\Rightarrow$ (3), suppose that $F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq 0})$ and $\tau_{\leq n} F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ is compact for each $n$. Then, by assumption $\tau_{\leq 0} F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Ab}) \subset \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq 0})$ is a compact object and thus $\pi_0 F$ is a finitely generated functor. We can thus find a functor $G \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq 0})$ which is a direct sum of $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(X, \cdot)$, for finitely many $X\in\mathcal C$, and a map $G \to F$ which is a surjection on $\pi_0$. Let $F_1 $ be the resulting cofiber and observe that $F_1$ has the same property as $F$ (namely $\tau_{\leq n} F_1 \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ is compact for each $n$, since compact objects are closed under pushouts) and that $F_1 $ is connected. Continuing in this way, we find a sequence of functors $F \to F_1 \to F_2 \to \dots $ such that $F_n$ is concentrated in degrees $\geq n$ and such that the cofiber of each $F_n \to F_{n+1}$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of representables. We obtain the desired sequence $G_n$ by setting $G_n=\operatorname{Fib}(F\to F_{n+1})$. For (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1), note that each $G_n$ is perfect by induction on $n$, and that $G_{n+1}\rightarrow F$ is an equivalence on $\tau_{\leq n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Cyclic implications: truncation preserves compacts; build the filtration by iterated $\pi_0$-surjections; induct back.

nodes.name: (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2): truncation preserves compact objects
nodes.statement: For (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2), suppose that $F\in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ (we do not need $F$ connective) is pseudocoherent and let $n\in\mathbb Z$. Then by definition there is a perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to F$ inducing an equivalence $\tau_{\leq n} F' \simeq \tau_{\leq n} F$. Since $\tau_{\leq n}: \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp) \to \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ preserves compact objects (as its right adjoint preserves filtered colimits), it follows that $\tau_{\leq n} F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ is compact.
nodes.statement_short: Truncate the perfect approximation and use that $\tau_{\leq n}$ preserves compacts.

nodes.name: (2) $\Rightarrow$ (3): build the filtration by killing $\pi_0$
nodes.statement: For (2) $\Rightarrow$ (3), suppose that $F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq 0})$ and $\tau_{\leq n} F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ is compact for each $n$. Then, by assumption $\tau_{\leq 0} F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \mathrm{Ab}) \subset \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq 0})$ is a compact object and thus $\pi_0 F$ is a finitely generated functor. We can thus find a functor $G \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq 0})$ which is a direct sum of $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(X, \cdot)$, for finitely many $X\in\mathcal C$, and a map $G \to F$ which is a surjection on $\pi_0$. Let $F_1 $ be the resulting cofiber and observe that $F_1$ has the same property as $F$ (namely $\tau_{\leq n} F_1 \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\leq n})$ is compact for each $n$, since compact objects are closed under pushouts) and that $F_1 $ is connected. Continuing in this way, we find a sequence of functors $F \to F_1 \to F_2 \to \dots $ such that $F_n$ is concentrated in degrees $\geq n$ and such that the cofiber of each $F_n \to F_{n+1}$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of representables. We obtain the desired sequence $G_n$ by setting $G_n=\operatorname{Fib}(F\to F_{n+1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Iteratively cover $\pi_0$ by finitely many corepresentables to build the filtration.

nodes.name: (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1): each stage is perfect
nodes.statement: For (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1), note that each $G_n$ is perfect by induction on $n$, and that $G_{n+1}\rightarrow F$ is an equivalence on $\tau_{\leq n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Induct up the filtration to produce the required perfect approximations.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{D}$-perfect, $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, $\mathcal{D}$-finitely generated
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a small full subcategory of a (possibly large, but locally small) category $\mathcal{C}$. Let $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ be a functor. \begin{enumerate} \item We say that $F$ is \emph{$\mathcal{D}$-perfect} if $F$ belongs to the thick subcategory of $\fun(\mathcal C,\Sp)$ generated by the functors $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot)$ for $D \in \mathcal{D}$. \item We say that a functor $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ is called \emph{$\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent} if for each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, there exists a $\mathcal{D}$-perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to F$ such that $\tau_{\leq n} F'(C) \to \tau_{\leq n} F(C)$ is an equivalence for all $C \in \mathcal{C}$. \item A functor $F_0: \mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ is called \emph{$\mathcal{D}$-finitely generated} if there is a surjection as in \eqref{fingenfun} with $X_i \in \mathcal{D}$ for each $i$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Relative versions of perfect/pseudocoherent/finitely generated, using only corepresentables from a subcategory $\mathcal{D}$.
differentia: for each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, there exists a $\mathcal{D}$-perfect functor $F'$ and a map $F' \to F$ such that $\tau_{\leq n} F'(C) \to \tau_{\leq n} F(C)$ is an equivalence for all $C \in \mathcal{C}$

nodes.name: left Kan extension and left Kan extended functors
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a full subcategory. Given a functor $G: \mathcal{D} \to \Sp$, we can form the \emph{left Kan extension} $\lan(G):\mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ (cf. \cite[Sec.~4.3]{HTT}). By definition, for $C \in \mathcal{C}$, $\lan(G)(C)$ is the colimit $$ \lan(G)(C) = \varinjlim_{D \to C, D \in \mathcal{D}} G(D) \in \Sp.$$ The construction $F \mapsto \lan(F)$ is the left adjoint of the forgetful functor $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp) \to \fun(\mathcal{D}, \Sp)$. A functor $F \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ is said to be \emph{left Kan extended} from $\mathcal{D}$ if the natural map $\lan( F|_{\mathcal{D}}) \to F$ is an equivalence in $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$. The objects of $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ which are left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$ form a subcategory equivalent to $\fun(\mathcal{D}, \Sp)$ (via restriction).
nodes.statement_short: Left Kan extension along $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ and the notion of a functor left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$.
differentia: the natural map $\lan( F|_{\mathcal{D}}) \to F$ is an equivalence in $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$

nodes.name: $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherence via left Kan extension
nodes.statement: A functor $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent if and only if it is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$ and $F|_{\mathcal{D}}: \mathcal{D} \to \Sp$ is pseudocoherent.
assumptions: A functor $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$
conclusions: is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent if and only if it is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$ and $F|_{\mathcal{D}}: \mathcal{D} \to \Sp$ is pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Proof of the Kan-extension criterion for $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherence
nodes.statement: The functor $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot) \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ for $D \in \mathcal{D}$ is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$, so a thick subcategory argument shows that any $\mathcal{D}$-perfect functor is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$. To get the same for any $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functor, note that the truncations $\Sp\rightarrow \Sp_{\leq n}$ are a conservative family of colimit-preserving functors, so a functor to $\Sp$ is left Kan extended if and only if its image in each $\Sp_{\leq n}$ is. Conversely, suppose that $F$ is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$ and $F|_{\mathcal{D}}: \mathcal{D} \to \Sp$ is pseudocoherent. Then $\tau_{\leq n}F\mid_\mathcal{D}\simeq \tau_{\leq n}G\mid_\mathcal{D}$ for some $G:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\Sp$ in the thick subcategory generated by the $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot)$, and we deduce $\tau_{\leq n}F\simeq \tau_{\leq n}G$ by left Kan extension.
nodes.statement_short: Thick-subcategory argument in one direction; transport truncated equivalences along Kan extension in the other.

nodes.name: Forward direction: $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent implies left Kan extended
nodes.statement: The functor $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot) \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ for $D \in \mathcal{D}$ is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$, so a thick subcategory argument shows that any $\mathcal{D}$-perfect functor is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$. To get the same for any $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functor, note that the truncations $\Sp\rightarrow \Sp_{\leq n}$ are a conservative family of colimit-preserving functors, so a functor to $\Sp$ is left Kan extended if and only if its image in each $\Sp_{\leq n}$ is.
nodes.statement_short: Thick subcategory argument plus conservativity of truncations.

nodes.name: Converse direction via truncated comparison
nodes.statement: Conversely, suppose that $F$ is left Kan extended from $\mathcal{D}$ and $F|_{\mathcal{D}}: \mathcal{D} \to \Sp$ is pseudocoherent. Then $\tau_{\leq n}F\mid_\mathcal{D}\simeq \tau_{\leq n}G\mid_\mathcal{D}$ for some $G:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\Sp$ in the thick subcategory generated by the $\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot)$, and we deduce $\tau_{\leq n}F\simeq \tau_{\leq n}G$ by left Kan extension.
nodes.statement_short: Extend the truncated equivalence from $\mathcal{D}$ to $\mathcal{C}$.

nodes.name: Filtration criterion for $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherence
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a small full subcategory. Let $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq d}$ be a functor for some $d \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. \item There exists a sequence $G_{d-1} = 0 \to G_d \to G_{d+1} \to G_{d+2} \to \dots $ such that $G_i/G_{i-1}$ is a finite direct sum of functors of the form $\Sigma^i \Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot)$ for $D \in \mathcal{D}$ and such that $\varinjlim_i G_i \simeq F$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a small full subcategory.
Let $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq d}$ be a functor for some $d \in \mathbb{Z}$.
conclusions: $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.

There exists a sequence $G_{d-1} = 0 \to G_d \to G_{d+1} \to G_{d+2} \to \dots $ such that $G_i/G_{i-1}$ is a finite direct sum of functors of the form $\Sigma^i \Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(D, \cdot)$ for $D \in \mathcal{D}$ and such that $\varinjlim_i G_i \simeq F$.

nodes.name: Proof of the filtration criterion
nodes.statement: Combine Lemmas~\ref{lkanpscoh} and \ref{pscohcompact}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two earlier criteria.

nodes.name: Closure properties of $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ a small full subcategory. \begin{enumerate} \item The subcategory of $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ spanned by the $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors is thick. \item Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$, let $K$ be a simplicial set, and let $f: K \to \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq d})$ be a $K$-indexed diagram of functors $\mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq d}$. Suppose that the $n$-skeleton $\mathrm{sk}_n K$ is a finite simplicial set for every $n\in\mathbb Z$ and that for each vertex $k_0 \in K_0$, the functor $f(k_0) \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. Then the functor $\varinjlim_K f \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. \item Let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$, and let $F_\bullet:\Delta^\sub{op}\to \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp_{\geq d})$ be a simplicial object in the category of functors $\mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq d}$. Suppose that $F_i$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent for every $i \geq 0$. Then the geometric realization $|F_\bullet|: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. \item Let $d\in \bb Z$, and let $F\in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ be a $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functor such that $\pi_nF=0$ for all $n<d$. Then $\pi_d F: \mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ is a $\mathcal{D}$-finitely generated functor. \item If $\mathcal{C}$ has finite coproducts and $\mathcal{D}$ is closed under them, then the subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors in $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ is closed under smash products. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors form a thick subcategory closed under finite-skeleton colimits, geometric realizations, and smash products, with finitely generated bottom homotopy.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ a small full subcategory.
conclusions: The subcategory of $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ spanned by the $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors is thick.
Then the functor $\varinjlim_K f \in \fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
Then the geometric realization $|F_\bullet|: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
Then $\pi_d F: \mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ is a $\mathcal{D}$-finitely generated functor.
the subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors in $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \Sp)$ is closed under smash products

nodes.name: Proof of the closure properties
nodes.statement: Thanks to Lemma~\ref{lkanpscoh}, we may assume without loss of generality that $\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{D}$, since the property of being left Kan extended is preserved under all colimits. We may also take $d = 0$. Claim (1) follows from Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact} because compact objects (of any $\infty$-category) are closed under finite colimits and retracts. For (2), it suffices by Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact} to show that $\tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_K f )$ is compact as an object of $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \sp_{\leq n})$ for each $n$. But $\tau_{\leq n} f = \tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_{\mathrm{sk}^{n+1} K } f)$ and $\varinjlim_{\mathrm{sk}^{n+1} K } f$ is a finite colimit of pseudocoherent functors, hence pseudocoherent itself by (1); this implies the desired compactness assertion. Claim (3) is handled similarly, because $\tau_{\leq n} ( |F_\bullet|) \simeq \tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_{\Delta_{\leq n+1} }F)$ can be computed as a truncated geometric realization, and this is a finite colimit, cf.~\cite[Lemma~1.2.4.17]{HA}. Claim (4) follows from the filtration Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact}. For (5), it suffices to observe that the smash products of functors of the form $\{\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(X, \cdot)\}_{X \in \mathcal{D}}$ are still of this form under the assumption that $\mathcal{C}$ has finite coproducts and $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ is closed under them. It then follows by a thick subcategory argument that the subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$-perfect functors is closed under smash products, which implies the analogous assertion for $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{D}$ and verify each claim from the truncated compactness criterion.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{D}$ and $d=0$
nodes.statement: Thanks to Lemma~\ref{lkanpscoh}, we may assume without loss of generality that $\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{D}$, since the property of being left Kan extended is preserved under all colimits. We may also take $d = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalize the setting using the Kan-extension criterion.

nodes.name: Claim (1): thickness from compactness
nodes.statement: Claim (1) follows from Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact} because compact objects (of any $\infty$-category) are closed under finite colimits and retracts.
nodes.statement_short: Compact objects are closed under finite colimits and retracts.

nodes.name: Claims (2) and (3): skeletal and truncated realizations are finite colimits
nodes.statement: For (2), it suffices by Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact} to show that $\tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_K f )$ is compact as an object of $\fun(\mathcal{C}, \sp_{\leq n})$ for each $n$. But $\tau_{\leq n} f = \tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_{\mathrm{sk}^{n+1} K } f)$ and $\varinjlim_{\mathrm{sk}^{n+1} K } f$ is a finite colimit of pseudocoherent functors, hence pseudocoherent itself by (1); this implies the desired compactness assertion. Claim (3) is handled similarly, because $\tau_{\leq n} ( |F_\bullet|) \simeq \tau_{\leq n} ( \varinjlim_{\Delta_{\leq n+1} }F)$ can be computed as a truncated geometric realization, and this is a finite colimit, cf.~\cite[Lemma~1.2.4.17]{HA}.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate the colimit by its $(n+1)$-skeleton, a finite colimit.

nodes.name: Claims (4) and (5): bottom homotopy and smash products
nodes.statement: Claim (4) follows from the filtration Lemma~\ref{pscohcompact}. For (5), it suffices to observe that the smash products of functors of the form $\{\Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\mathcal{C}}(X, \cdot)\}_{X \in \mathcal{D}}$ are still of this form under the assumption that $\mathcal{C}$ has finite coproducts and $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ is closed under them. It then follows by a thick subcategory argument that the subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$-perfect functors is closed under smash products, which implies the analogous assertion for $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors.
nodes.statement_short: Read off (4) from the filtration and (5) from stability of corepresentables under smash product.

nodes.name: Goodwillie tower of $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty$
nodes.statement: There is a natural tower $\left\{P_n=P_n ( \Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)\right\}_{n \geq 0}$ of functors $\Sp \to \Sp$ receiving a map from $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty$, \[ \Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty X \to \{ \dots \to P_n (X) \to P_{n-1}(X) \to \dots \to P_1(X) \} \] such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $P_1(X) \simeq X$ and the fiber of $P_n (X) \to P_{n-1} (X) $ is naturally equivalent to $(X^{\otimes n})_{h \Sigma_n}$. \item If $X \in \Sp_{\geq 1}$, the map $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty X \to \varprojlim_n P_n (X)$ is an equivalence and the connectivity of $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty X \to P_n(X)$ tends to $\infty$ with $n$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: The Goodwillie tower of $\Sigma^\infty\Omega^\infty$ has layers $(X^{\otimes n})_{h\Sigma_n}$ and converges on $\Sp_{\geq 1}$.
conclusions: There is a natural tower $\left\{P_n=P_n ( \Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)\right\}_{n \geq 0}$ of functors $\Sp \to \Sp$ receiving a map from $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty$
$P_1(X) \simeq X$ and the fiber of $P_n (X) \to P_{n-1} (X) $ is naturally equivalent to $(X^{\otimes n})_{h \Sigma_n}$.

If $X \in \Sp_{\geq 1}$, the map $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty X \to \varprojlim_n P_n (X)$ is an equivalence and the connectivity of $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty X \to P_n(X)$ tends to $\infty$ with $n$.

nodes.name: Pseudocoherence is detected by $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category with finite coproducts and let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a small subcategory closed under finite coproducts. Let $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq 1}$ a functor. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. \item $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. \item $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For functors into $\Sp_{\geq 1}$, pseudocoherence of $F$ and of $\Sigma^\infty\Omega^\infty F$ are equivalent.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category with finite coproducts and let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a small subcategory closed under finite coproducts.
Let $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq 1}$ a functor.
conclusions: $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
$\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
$\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.

nodes.name: Proof that $\Sigma^\infty\Omega^\infty$ detects pseudocoherence
nodes.statement: The equivalence of (2) and (3) follows because $\Sigma^\infty, \Sigma^\infty_+$ differ by the constant functor at $S^0$, which is corepresentable since $\mathcal{C}$ has an initial object in $\mathcal{D}$. Suppose $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. Using Proposition~\ref{goodwilliefilt}, we conclude that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is the homotopy limit of a tower whose associated graded is given by $F, (F^{\otimes 2})_{h \Sigma_2}, (F^{\otimes 3})_{h \Sigma_3 }, \dots $. Since $F$ takes values in $\Sp_{\geq 1}$, the connectivity of the associated graded terms tends to $\infty$, so this tower stabilizes in any given finite range. As $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, so are all the graded terms in view of Proposition~\ref{general:pscoh}. It follows that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. Conversely, suppose $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. First, recall that the adjunction $(\Sigma^\infty, \Omega^\infty)$ between the $\infty$-categories of pointed spaces and connective spectra is monadic since $\Omega^\infty|_{\Sp_{\geq 0}}$ commutes with sifted colimits \cite[Prop.~1.4.3.9]{HA} and in view of the $\infty$-categorical monadicity theorem \cite[Sec.~4.7.3]{HA}; alternatively, this follows explicitly from delooping machinery going back to \cite{Maygeom}. As a result of monadicity, for any $X \in \Sp_{\geq 0}$, one has a natural simplicial spectrum (the bar resolution) $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^{\bullet + 1} X$ whose geometric realization is equivalent to $X$. Therefore, in our case, we can resolve $F$ via the iterates $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^k F$ for $k \geq 1$. By the previous direction and our assumption, each of these is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. Thus we have written $F$ as a geometric realization of $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors $\mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq 1}$, so $F$ itself is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Use the Goodwillie tower forwards and the monadic bar resolution of $(\Sigma^\infty,\Omega^\infty)$ backwards.

nodes.name: Equivalence of (2) and (3)
nodes.statement: The equivalence of (2) and (3) follows because $\Sigma^\infty, \Sigma^\infty_+$ differ by the constant functor at $S^0$, which is corepresentable since $\mathcal{C}$ has an initial object in $\mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Sigma^\infty$ and $\Sigma^\infty_+$ differ by a corepresentable constant.

nodes.name: (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2) via the Goodwillie tower
nodes.statement: Suppose $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. Using Proposition~\ref{goodwilliefilt}, we conclude that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is the homotopy limit of a tower whose associated graded is given by $F, (F^{\otimes 2})_{h \Sigma_2}, (F^{\otimes 3})_{h \Sigma_3 }, \dots $. Since $F$ takes values in $\Sp_{\geq 1}$, the connectivity of the associated graded terms tends to $\infty$, so this tower stabilizes in any given finite range. As $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, so are all the graded terms in view of Proposition~\ref{general:pscoh}. It follows that $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: The Goodwillie layers are pseudocoherent and the tower stabilizes in each range.

nodes.name: (2) $\Rightarrow$ (1) via the monadic bar resolution
nodes.statement: Conversely, suppose $\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. First, recall that the adjunction $(\Sigma^\infty, \Omega^\infty)$ between the $\infty$-categories of pointed spaces and connective spectra is monadic since $\Omega^\infty|_{\Sp_{\geq 0}}$ commutes with sifted colimits \cite[Prop.~1.4.3.9]{HA} and in view of the $\infty$-categorical monadicity theorem \cite[Sec.~4.7.3]{HA}; alternatively, this follows explicitly from delooping machinery going back to \cite{Maygeom}. As a result of monadicity, for any $X \in \Sp_{\geq 0}$, one has a natural simplicial spectrum (the bar resolution) $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^{\bullet + 1} X$ whose geometric realization is equivalent to $X$. Therefore, in our case, we can resolve $F$ via the iterates $(\Sigma^\infty \Omega^\infty)^k F$ for $k \geq 1$. By the previous direction and our assumption, each of these is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. Thus we have written $F$ as a geometric realization of $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent functors $\mathcal{C} \to \Sp_{\geq 1}$, so $F$ itself is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Resolve $F$ by iterates of $\Sigma^\infty\Omega^\infty$ and use closure under geometric realization.

nodes.name: Pseudocoherence can be tested after smashing with $H\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a small subcategory. Let $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ be a functor. If $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, then $H\mathbb{Z} \otimes F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent. Conversely, if $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ is uniformly bounded-below and $H \mathbb{Z} \otimes F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, so is $F$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ be a small subcategory.
Let $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ be a functor.
conclusions: If $F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, then $H\mathbb{Z} \otimes F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent.
Conversely, if $F: \mathcal{C} \to \Sp$ is uniformly bounded-below and $H \mathbb{Z} \otimes F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, so is $F$.

nodes.name: Proof that $H\mathbb{Z}$-homology detects pseudocoherence
nodes.statement: The first direction follows because we can approximate $H \mathbb{Z}$ in any range by a finite spectrum. The second direction follows because a thick subcategory argument now implies that if $H \mathbb{Z} \otimes F$ is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent, so is $\tau_{\leq n} S^0 \otimes F$ for each $n$, and we can approximate $F$ in any given range by $\tau_{\leq n} S^0 \otimes F$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $H\mathbb{Z}$ by finite spectra one way, and $S^0$ by its truncations the other.

nodes.name: projectively finitely generated / projectively pseudocoherent
nodes.statement:
egin{enumerate} \item A functor $
uh 	o \mathrm{Ab}$ is \emph{projectively finitely generated} if it is $\mathcal{D}$-finitely generated for $\mathcal{D} = (
uh)_{\Sigma}$. \item A functor $
uh 	o \Sp$ is \emph{projectively pseudocoherent} if it is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent for $\mathcal{D} = (
uh)_\Sigma$. \end{enumerate}
differentia: it is $\mathcal{D}$-pseudocoherent for $\mathcal{D} = (\nuh)_\Sigma$

nodes.name: The corepresentable functors $I \mapsto \Sigma^\infty_+ I^n$
nodes.statement: For each $n$, the functor $I \mapsto \Sigma^\infty_+ I^n$ (where $I^n$ here denotes the cartesian product of $n$ copies of $I$) is projectively pseudocoherent. Indeed, it is the suspension spectrum of the corepresentable associated to $ R\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}^+ \in (\nuh)_\Sigma$.

nodes.name: Projectively pseudocoherent functors are finitary
nodes.statement: A projectively pseudocoherent functor $\nuh \to \Sp$ commutes with filtered colimits. In fact, the corepresentable functors $I \mapsto \Sigma^\infty_+ I^n$ clearly do, and the result for arbitrary projectively pseudocoherent functors follows because the class of functors $\nuh \to \Sp$ which commute with filtered colimits is stable under all colimits. See also Corollary~\ref{kanextcrit} below.

nodes.name: Gabber's vanishing lemma for projectively finitely generated functors
nodes.statement:
Let $F_0: 
uzh 	o \mathrm{Ab}$ be a projectively finitely generated functor. Suppose that:  egin{enumerate} \item $F_0(I) = 0$ if $I \in 
uzh$ is annihilated by an integer $N > 0$. \item $F_0(I) = 0$ if $I \in 
uzh$ is a nonunital $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra. \item Given a short exact sequence $I' 	o I 	woheadrightarrow \overline{I}$ in $
uzh$, the sequence $F_0(I') 	o F_0(I) 	o F_0(\overline{I}) 	o 0$ of abelian groups is exact. \item $F_0$ commutes with filtered colimits. \end{enumerate} Then $F_0 = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: A projectively finitely generated functor vanishing on torsion and on $\mathbb{Q}$-algebras, right exact and finitary, is zero.
assumptions: Let $F_0: \nuzh \to \mathrm{Ab}$ be a projectively finitely generated functor.
$F_0(I) = 0$ if $I \in \nuzh$ is annihilated by an integer $N > 0$.
$F_0(I) = 0$ if $I \in \nuzh$ is a nonunital $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra.
Given a short exact sequence $I' \to I \twoheadrightarrow \overline{I}$ in $\nuzh$, the sequence $F_0(I') \to F_0(I) \to F_0(\overline{I}) \to 0$ of abelian groups is exact.
$F_0$ commutes with filtered colimits.
conclusions: Then $F_0 = 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Gabber's vanishing lemma
nodes.statement_short: Find one $N$ killing all generators via the $\mathbb{Q}$-vanishing and finitariness, then show $F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)$ is zero.

nodes.name: Reduce the lemma to a claim about $i_N: NI \to I$
nodes.statement: We will prove the following claim: there exists $N\ge1$ such that, for any $I \in \nuzh$, the inclusion map $i_N:NI\to I$ induces the zero map $0=(i_N)_*: F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)$. Once this is done, the statement of the lemma will follow by applying (1) and (3) to the short exact sequence $NI\to I\to I/NI$.
nodes.statement_short: State the key claim and show it implies the lemma.

nodes.name: Kill any single class by a multiplication operator $[N]$
nodes.statement: As in Corollary~\ref{rationalhens}, let $[N]: \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$ be the operator that multiplies each $x_i$ by $N$, so that the colimit of the $[N]$, indexed over $N\ge1$ ordered by divisibility, is $\mathbb{Q}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+$. By assumption $F_0$ commutes with filtered colimits and annihilates any nonunital henselian $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra; so, given any element $u \in F_0(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+)$, it follows that there exists $N > 0$ such that $[N]_*(u) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\mathbb{Q}$-vanishing plus finitariness to kill each class by some $[N]$.

nodes.name: Use projective finite generation to get finitely many generators
nodes.statement_short: Identify universal generators $g_i$ from the presenting surjection.

nodes.name: Conclude: every map into $NI$ factors through $[N]$
nodes.statement:
By the second paragraph, there exists an integer $N > 0$ such that $[N]_*(g_i)=0$ for all the generators $g_i$. From this we can easily complete the proof of the claim, as follows. Given any $I \in 
uzh$, every map $\phi: \mathbb{Z}\{ x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}\}^+ 	o N I $ has the property that the composite $i_N \circ \phi: \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}ight\}^+ 	o I$ factors through $[N]$, i.e., one has a commutative diagram in $
uzh$ \[ \xymatrix{ \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_night\}^+ \ar[r]_-{\phi}\ar[d]^{[N]} & NI \ar[d]^{i_N} \ \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_night\}^+ \ar[r] & I }.\] By choice of $N$ it follows that the composite \[ \mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Hom}_{
uzh}( \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}ight\}^+, NI)] 	o F_0(NI) 	o F_0(I) \] is zero. But we have shown that every element of $F_0(NI)$ is a finite sum of elements of the form $\phi_*(g_i)$ for various maps $\phi$. Since $g_i \in F_0( \mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n_i}ight\}^+)$ is annihilated by $[N]$, it follows that $(i_N)_*: F_0(NI) 	o F_0(I)$ is zero, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Factor every map into $NI$ through $[N]$ to kill the whole of $F_0(NI) \to F_0(I)$.

nodes.name: Axiomatic rigidity argument
nodes.statement:
Let $F: 
uzh 	o \Sp$ be a projectively pseudocoherent functor. Suppose that:  egin{enumerate} \item For each prime field $R$ and each $n$, we have $F( R\left\{x_1, \dots, x_night\}^+) = 0$. \item Given a short exact sequence $I' 	o I 	woheadrightarrow \overline{I}$ in $
uzh$, the sequence $F(I') 	o F(I) 	o F(\overline{I})$ is a fiber sequence of spectra. \item If $I \in 
uzh$ is nilpotent, then $F(I) = 0$. \end{enumerate} Then $F = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: A projectively pseudocoherent, excisive functor vanishing on free objects over prime fields and on nilpotents is zero.
assumptions: Let $F: \nuzh \to \Sp$ be a projectively pseudocoherent functor.
For each prime field $R$ and each $n$, we have $F( R\left\{x_1, \dots, x_n\right\}^+) = 0$.
Given a short exact sequence $I' \to I \twoheadrightarrow \overline{I}$ in $\nuzh$, the sequence $F(I') \to F(I) \to F(\overline{I})$ is a fiber sequence of spectra.
If $I \in \nuzh$ is nilpotent, then $F(I) = 0$.
conclusions: Then $F = 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of the axiomatic rigidity argument
nodes.statement:
Let $R$ be a prime field and restrict $F$ to $
uh$ to obtain a functor $F_R: 
uh 	o \Sp$. We observe first that $F_R$ is projectively pseudocoherent (since the building blocks $I \mapsto \Sigma^\infty_+ I^n$ for projectively pseudocoherent functors $
uh 	o \Sp$ are independent of the base ring $R$). In particular, $F_R$ is left Kan extended from the subcategory $(
uh)_{\Sigma}$. By assumption, $F_R$ annihilates $(
uh)_\Sigma$, so that $F_R = 0$ on $
uh$. It follows that $F$ annihilates any nonunital henselian algebra over a field. Moreover, if $I \in 
uzh$ is such that there exists $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ with $NI = 0$, it follows that $F(I) = 0$: in fact, since $F$ preserves finite products we reduce to the case where $N = p^r$ for some $r$, and then use the short exact sequence $pI 	o I 	o I/p I$ where $pI$ is nilpotent. The resulting fiber sequence then shows that $F(I) \simeq F(I/pI) = 0$. Suppose $F$ is not the zero functor. Let $d$ be minimal such that $\pi_d F 
eq 0$. Then $\pi_d F$ is a projectively finitely generated functor $
uzh 	o \mathrm{Ab}$ which commutes with filtered colimits; furthermore, $\pi_d F$ annihilates any $I \in 
uzh$ which is either of bounded torsion or a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space. Using Lemma~ef{gabberlem} below, we find that $\pi_d F = 0$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Kill $F$ on henselian algebras over fields, then on bounded-torsion objects, then contradict minimality of $d$ using Gabber's lemma.

nodes.name: Vanishing over a prime field via left Kan extension
nodes.statement:
Let $R$ be a prime field and restrict $F$ to $
uh$ to obtain a functor $F_R: 
uh 	o \Sp$. We observe first that $F_R$ is projectively pseudocoherent (since the building blocks $I \mapsto \Sigma^\infty_+ I^n$ for projectively pseudocoherent functors $
uh 	o \Sp$ are independent of the base ring $R$). In particular, $F_R$ is left Kan extended from the subcategory $(
uh)_{\Sigma}$. By assumption, $F_R$ annihilates $(
uh)_\Sigma$, so that $F_R = 0$ on $
uh$.
nodes.statement_short: Left Kan extension from the free objects forces $F_R = 0$ over a prime field.

nodes.name: Vanishing on bounded-torsion nonunital rings
nodes.statement: It follows that $F$ annihilates any nonunital henselian algebra over a field. Moreover, if $I \in \nuzh$ is such that there exists $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ with $NI = 0$, it follows that $F(I) = 0$: in fact, since $F$ preserves finite products we reduce to the case where $N = p^r$ for some $r$, and then use the short exact sequence $pI \to I \to I/p I$ where $pI$ is nilpotent. The resulting fiber sequence then shows that $F(I) \simeq F(I/pI) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the excision fiber sequence and nilpotent vanishing to handle $N$-torsion objects.

nodes.name: Contradict minimality of $d$ via the Gabber vanishing lemma
nodes.statement:
Suppose $F$ is not the zero functor. Let $d$ be minimal such that $\pi_d F 
eq 0$. Then $\pi_d F$ is a projectively finitely generated functor $
uzh 	o \mathrm{Ab}$ which commutes with filtered colimits; furthermore, $\pi_d F$ annihilates any $I \in 
uzh$ which is either of bounded torsion or a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space. Using Lemma~ef{gabberlem} below, we find that $\pi_d F = 0$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the abelian vanishing lemma to the lowest nonzero homotopy functor.

nodes.name: Computing left Kan extended functors by simplicial resolutions
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be an $\infty$-category that has sifted colimits, fix a base ring $R$ and a functor \[ F: 
uh 	o \mathcal{E}, \] and consider the following condition on $F$:  egin{itemize} \item[(Kan)] $F$ is left Kan extended from the subcatgory $(
uh)_\Sigma \subset 
uh$. \end{itemize} Suppose $F$ satisfies (Kan). Then one can compute $F$ from its values on $(
uh)_\Sigma$ as follows. First, $F$ commutes with filtered colimits, and hence its value is determined on all free objects in $
uh$. Next, if $I$ is an arbitrary nonunital henselian $R$-algebra, then there exists an augmented simplicial object $I_ ullet:\Delta^\sub{op}_+ 	o 
uh$ such that $I_{-1} = I$, each $I_i$ is a free algebra in $
uh$, and $|I_ ullet| \simeq I_{-1} = I$, i.e., $I_ ullet$ is a simplicial resolution of $I$ by free objects; then the value of $F$ on $I$ is given by $F(I) = |F(I_ ullet)|$. The construction of such simplicial resolutions (and the independence of choices) is a general homotopical technique going back to Quillen \cite{QuillenHA}, originally developed to build the cotangent complex via simplicial commutative rings. Using the results of \cite{QuillenHA} (which work in particular for any category satisfying (Law) from Remark ef{remark_Lawvere}, by \cite[Rmk.~1, pg.~II.4.2]{QuillenHA}), we can make the category $ un( \Delta^\sub{op}, 
ur)$ of simplicial nonunital henselian $R$-algebras into a model category where the weak equivalences and fibrations are those of underlying simplicial sets. The resolution $I_ ullet$ of $I$ is then obtained as a cofibrant replacement in this model category of the constant simplicial object $I$. This can also be phrased using the language of nonabelian derived $\infty$-categories \cite[Sec.~5.5.8]{HTT}. We record these observations for the future in the following corollary which does not mention simplicial non-unital henselian rings.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (Kan) lets one compute $F$ from free objects via simplicial resolutions, following Quillen.

nodes.name: Criterion for being left Kan extended from $(\nuh)_\Sigma$
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be an $\infty$-category with sifted colimits, and let $F: 
uh 	o \mathcal{E}$ be a functor. Then the following are equivalent:  egin{enumerate} \item $F$ is left Kan extended from $(
uh)_{\Sigma} \subset 
uh$. \item Whenever $I_ ullet$ is a simplicial object in $
uh$ whose geometric realization is equivalent to $I_{-1} \in 
uh$ (in particular, the homotopy type of the underlying simplicial set of $I_ ullet$ is discrete), then the map $|F(I_ ullet)| 	o F(I_{-1})$ is an equivalence. ootnote{Since the category of nonunital henselian rings is the category of algebras over a monad on the category of sets, there is always a canonical resolution of any object by free objects; it would suffice to consider these resolutions.} Furthermore, $F$ commutes with filtered colimits. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Being left Kan extended from the free objects is equivalent to preserving simplicial resolutions and filtered colimits.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be an $\infty$-category with sifted colimits, and let $F: \nuh \to \mathcal{E}$ be a functor.
conclusions: $F$ is left Kan extended from $(\nuh)_{\Sigma} \subset \nuh$.

Whenever $I_\bullet$ is a simplicial object in $\nuh$ whose geometric realization is equivalent to $I_{-1} \in \nuh$ (in particular, the homotopy type of the underlying simplicial set of $I_\bullet$ is discrete), then the map $|F(I_\bullet)| \to F(I_{-1})$ is an equivalence.\footnote{Since the category of nonunital henselian rings is the category of algebras over a monad on the category of sets, there is always a canonical resolution of any object by free objects; it would suffice to consider these resolutions.} Furthermore, $F$ commutes with filtered colimits.

nodes.name: Projective pseudocoherence of $I \mapsto C_*(BGL_\infty(\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I);\mathbb{Z})$
nodes.statement: The functor $ \nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto C_*( BGL_\infty(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent.
assumptions: The functor $ \nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto C_*( BGL_\infty(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$
conclusions: is projectively pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Proof of projective pseudocoherence of the $BGL_\infty$ chains
nodes.statement: First, by the homological stability results of Maazen and van der Kallen \cite{vdK}, we can approximate $C_*(BGL_\infty(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ by $C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ in any given finite range. It is crucial for us that this stability range is independent of the choice of $I$: namely, the stability range depends on the Krull dimension of the maximal spectrum of $\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I$, but since $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical this is the maximal spectrum of $\mathbb{Z}$. Thus, it suffices to show that for any $n$, the functor $I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent. We use the short exact sequence of groups \[ 1 \to GL_n(1 + I) \to GL_n( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I) \to GL_n(\mathbb{Z}) \to 1, \] where $GL_n(1 + I)$ is, by definition, the kernel of the second map in the above sequence. It follows that there is a $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-action on $C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ and we have \begin{equation} C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z}) \simeq C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})_{h GL_n(\mathbb{Z})}. \end{equation} We next argue that the functor $I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent. Note that as a set, $GL_n(1 + I)$ is naturally isomorphic to the cartesian product $I^{n^2}$ since $I$ is contained in the radical of $\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I$. Now we observe that using the classical bar construction and the isomorphism (of sets) $GL_n(1 + I) \simeq I^{n^2}$, that $C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ is a geometric realization of functors of the form $I \mapsto \mathbb{Z}[I^{n^2i}]$ for $i \geq 0$. Since the functor $I \mapsto \mathbb{Z}[I^{n^2i}] \simeq H \mathbb{Z} \otimes \Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\nuzh}(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n^2i}\right\}^+, I)$ is clearly projectively pseudocoherent, it follows that $I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(1 +I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent as desired. Finally, the group $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ admits a finite index normal subgroup $N \leq GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $BN$ has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex, by the existence of the Borel-Serre compactification (see \cite{Serresurvey} for a survey). Since $(-)_{hGL_n(\mathbb{Z})} \simeq ((-)_{hN})_{h(G/N)}$, we conclude by two applications of Proposition \ref{general:pscoh} that taking $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-homotopy orbits preserves projective pseudocoherence. Therefore, we conclude in view of the previous paragraph and \eqref{glnZorbit}.
nodes.statement_short: Use uniform homological stability to reduce to $GL_n$, present $C_*(BGL_n(1+I))$ by the bar construction, and pass to $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-orbits via Borel--Serre.

nodes.name: Reduce to $GL_n$ by uniform homological stability
nodes.statement: First, by the homological stability results of Maazen and van der Kallen \cite{vdK}, we can approximate $C_*(BGL_\infty(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ by $C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ in any given finite range. It is crucial for us that this stability range is independent of the choice of $I$: namely, the stability range depends on the Krull dimension of the maximal spectrum of $\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I$, but since $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical this is the maximal spectrum of $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Homological stability with $I$-independent range reduces to finite $n$.

nodes.name: Split off $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ via the congruence short exact sequence
nodes.statement: Thus, it suffices to show that for any $n$, the functor $I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent. We use the short exact sequence of groups \[ 1 \to GL_n(1 + I) \to GL_n( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I) \to GL_n(\mathbb{Z}) \to 1, \] where $GL_n(1 + I)$ is, by definition, the kernel of the second map in the above sequence. It follows that there is a $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-action on $C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ and we have \begin{equation} C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z}) \simeq C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})_{h GL_n(\mathbb{Z})}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Express the chains as $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-homotopy orbits of the congruence-subgroup chains.

nodes.name: Bar construction for $C_*(BGL_n(1+I);\mathbb{Z})$
nodes.statement: We next argue that the functor $I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent. Note that as a set, $GL_n(1 + I)$ is naturally isomorphic to the cartesian product $I^{n^2}$ since $I$ is contained in the radical of $\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I$. Now we observe that using the classical bar construction and the isomorphism (of sets) $GL_n(1 + I) \simeq I^{n^2}$, that $C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})$ is a geometric realization of functors of the form $I \mapsto \mathbb{Z}[I^{n^2i}]$ for $i \geq 0$. Since the functor $I \mapsto \mathbb{Z}[I^{n^2i}] \simeq H \mathbb{Z} \otimes \Sigma^\infty_+ \hom_{\nuzh}(\mathbb{Z}\left\{x_1, \dots, x_{n^2i}\right\}^+, I)$ is clearly projectively pseudocoherent, it follows that $I \mapsto C_*(BGL_n(1 +I); \mathbb{Z})$ is projectively pseudocoherent as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Realize the chains as a geometric realization of corepresentable functors $\mathbb{Z}[I^{n^2i}]$.

nodes.name: Homotopy orbits for $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ preserve pseudocoherence
nodes.statement: Finally, the group $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ admits a finite index normal subgroup $N \leq GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $BN$ has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex, by the existence of the Borel-Serre compactification (see \cite{Serresurvey} for a survey). Since $(-)_{hGL_n(\mathbb{Z})} \simeq ((-)_{hN})_{h(G/N)}$, we conclude by two applications of Proposition \ref{general:pscoh} that taking $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-homotopy orbits preserves projective pseudocoherence. Therefore, we conclude in view of the previous paragraph and \eqref{glnZorbit}.
nodes.statement_short: Use Borel--Serre finiteness of $BN$ and the closure properties to descend to $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-orbits.

nodes.name: $C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I))$ as $GL_n(\mathbb{Z})$-homotopy orbits
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} C_*(BGL_n(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z}) \simeq C_*(BGL_n(1 + I); \mathbb{Z})_{h GL_n(\mathbb{Z})}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: $K_0$ invariance for a henselian pair
nodes.statement: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair. Then $K_0(R) \simeq K_0(R/I)$.
assumptions: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair.
conclusions: Then $K_0(R) \simeq K_0(R/I)$.

nodes.name: Proof of $K_0$ invariance
nodes.statement: In fact, we claim that isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective $R$ modules and isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective $R/I$-modules agree. For one direction, if $M, N$ are finitely generated projective $R$-modules, then any isomorphism $M/IM \simeq N/IM$ can be lifted to a map $M \to N$, which is necessarily an isomorphism by Nakayama's lemma applied to the kernel; we use here that $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $R$. For the other direction, by lifting idempotents any projective $R/I$-module lifts to $R$, cf. \cite[Tag 0D49]{stacks-project}.
nodes.statement_short: Match projective modules in both directions: lift isomorphisms by Nakayama, lift modules by lifting idempotents.

nodes.name: Lifting isomorphisms by Nakayama's lemma
nodes.statement: For one direction, if $M, N$ are finitely generated projective $R$-modules, then any isomorphism $M/IM \simeq N/IM$ can be lifted to a map $M \to N$, which is necessarily an isomorphism by Nakayama's lemma applied to the kernel; we use here that $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $R$.
nodes.statement_short: Lift an isomorphism mod $I$ and conclude by Nakayama.

nodes.name: Lifting projective modules by lifting idempotents
nodes.statement: For the other direction, by lifting idempotents any projective $R/I$-module lifts to $R$, cf. \cite[Tag 0D49]{stacks-project}.
nodes.statement_short: Lift idempotents to lift projective modules.

nodes.name: Projective pseudocoherence of $I \mapsto K(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)$
nodes.statement: The functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto K( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)$ is projectively pseudocoherent.
nodes.statement_short: Connective $K$-theory of $\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I$ is a projectively pseudocoherent functor of $I$.
assumptions: The functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto K( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)$
conclusions: is projectively pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Proof of projective pseudocoherence of $K$
nodes.statement: Since $I$ is henselian, we have $K_0( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I) = \mathbb{Z}$ by Lemma \ref{K0invhenspair}; since the constant functor $\mathbb{Z}$ is projectively pseudocoherent, it remains to see that the functor $I \mapsto \tau_{\geq 1} K(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)$ is projectively pseudocoherent. By Propositions \ref{suspensionpscoh} and \ref{HZpscoh} and the plus-construction description of $K$-theory (cf.~\cite[IV.1]{KBook} for an account), it suffices to check that the functor \[I \mapsto H \mathbb{Z} \otimes \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega^\infty \tau_{\geq 1} K(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I) \simeq C_*(BGL_\infty(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I); \mathbb{Z})\] is projectively pseudocoherent, which follows from Proposition~\ref{glpscoh} above.
nodes.statement_short: Split off $K_0 = \mathbb{Z}$, then reduce via the plus construction and the $\Sigma^\infty\Omega^\infty$/$H\mathbb{Z}$ criteria to the $BGL_\infty$ chains.

nodes.name: $K(\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I)$ commutes with simplicial resolutions
nodes.statement: In particular, Proposition \ref{Kpscoh} shows that the functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$, $I \mapsto K( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)$ commutes with simplicial resolutions in view of Construction~\ref{kanextsifted}. The same argument shows that this also holds in the larger category of nonunital local rings, even without the henselian condition. This observation, in various forms, plays an important role in the study of the local structure of $K$-theory. Compare, for instance \cite[Lemma I.2.2]{Goodrel} for the nilpotent case and \cite[Ch.~III, Prop.~1.4.2]{dgm} for a more general assertion for radical pairs.

nodes.name: Projective pseudocoherence of the Eilenberg--MacLane functor
nodes.statement: The Eilenberg--MacLane functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto HI$ is projectively pseudocoherent.
assumptions: The Eilenberg--MacLane functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto HI$
conclusions: is projectively pseudocoherent

nodes.name: $A \mapsto HA$ is $\mathrm{Latt}$-pseudocoherent
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{Ab}$ be the category of abelian groups. The functor $\mathrm{Ab} \to \Sp$ given by $A \mapsto HA$ is $\mathrm{Latt}$-pseudocoherent for $\mathrm{Latt} \subset \mathrm{Ab}$ the subcategory of finitely generated free abelian groups.
nodes.statement_short: The Eilenberg--MacLane functor on abelian groups is pseudocoherent relative to finitely generated free abelian groups.
assumptions: Let $\mathrm{Ab}$ be the category of abelian groups.
$\mathrm{Latt} \subset \mathrm{Ab}$ the subcategory of finitely generated free abelian groups
conclusions: The functor $\mathrm{Ab} \to \Sp$ given by $A \mapsto HA$ is $\mathrm{Latt}$-pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Proof that $A \mapsto HA$ is $\mathrm{Latt}$-pseudocoherent
nodes.statement: We can write functorially $HA = \varinjlim_n \Sigma^{-n}\Sigma^\infty K(A, n)$ for $K(A, n)$ the $n$th Eilenberg--MacLane space for $A$. This colimit stabilizes in any ranges of degrees by the Freudenthal suspension theorem, so it suffices to show that the functor $A \mapsto \Sigma^\infty K(A, n)$ is projectively pseudocoherent. But this follows from the iterated bar construction which gives a functorial model for $K(A, n)$ as the colimit of an $n$-fold simplicial space each of whose terms is a product of copies of $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $HA$ as a stabilizing colimit of $\Sigma^\infty K(A,n)$ and model $K(A,n)$ by the iterated bar construction.

nodes.name: Relation to Deligne's unpublished resolution result
nodes.statement: In the setting of $H\mathbb{Z}$-modules rather than spectra, Lemma~\ref{Abpscoh} is an unpublished result of Deligne, which states that any abelian group $A$ has a functorial resolution by free abelian groups all of whose terms are finite direct sums of the form $\mathbb{Z}[A^n]$. One can deduce Deligne's result from the above using the finiteness of the stable homotopy groups of spheres, and vice versa; compare Proposition \ref{HZpscoh}. For more discussion and a presentation of essentially the same argument in more classical terms of homological algebra, cf.~\cite[Appendix to Lec.~IV]{Condensed}.

nodes.name: Projective pseudocoherence of $I \mapsto \THH(\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I)$
nodes.statement: The functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto \THH( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)$ is projectively pseudocoherent.
assumptions: The functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto \THH( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)$
conclusions: is projectively pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Proof of projective pseudocoherence of $\THH$
nodes.statement: Using the cyclic bar construction for $\THH$, this follows because all the terms $(H(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I))^{\otimes k}$ (of which $\THH$ is a geometric realization) are projectively pseudocoherent in view of Lemma~\ref{EMpscoh} and Proposition~\ref{general:pscoh}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the closure properties to the cyclic bar construction for $\THH$.

nodes.name: Projective pseudocoherence of $I \mapsto \TC(\mathbb{Z}\ltimes I)/p$
nodes.statement: The functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto \TC( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)/p$ is projectively pseudocoherent.
assumptions: The functor $\nuzh \to \Sp$ given by $I \mapsto \TC( \mathbb{Z} \ltimes I)/p$
conclusions: is projectively pseudocoherent

nodes.name: Proof of projective pseudocoherence of $\TC/p$
nodes.statement: This now follows from Lemma~\ref{THHps} and Proposition~\ref{strong:finiteness}. Indeed, for any of the functors $F$ in the statement of the latter, we have that $I \mapsto F( \THH(\mathbb{Z} \ltimes I))$ is projectively pseudocoherent (note that taking $S^1$-homotopy orbits preserves pseudocoherence thanks to Lemma~\ref{general:pscoh}, as the skeleta of $BS^1$ are finite complexes), and then we can approximate $\TC/p$ in any range.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the $\THH$ lemma with the strong finiteness approximation of $\TC/p$ by $S^1$-homotopy-orbit functors.

nodes.name: $\nu^n(R) = \Omega^n_{R,\mathrm{log}}$ and $\widetilde{\nu^n}(R)$
nodes.statement: For an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $R$, we let $\nu^n(R) = \ker( 1 - C^{-1}: \Omega^n_R \to \Omega^n_R / d \Omega^{n-1}_R)$. We will also write this as $\Omega^n_{R, \mathrm{log}}$. We also let $\widetilde{\nu^n}(R)$ be the cokernel of $1 - C^{-1}$.
differentia: $\ker( 1 - C^{-1}: \Omega^n_R \to \Omega^n_R / d \Omega^{n-1}_R)$

nodes.name: Quasi-coherence of $\Omega^n$ and $\Omega^n/d\Omega^{n-1}$ under \'etale maps
nodes.statement: Let $R \to S$ be an \'etale map of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras. Let $R^{(1)} \rightarrow R, S^{(1)} \rightarrow S$ be the Frobenius twists of $R$ and $S$.\footnote{Thus $R^{(1)}$ consists of formal expressions of the form ``$a^p$", and the map to $R$ is ``$a^p$" $\mapsto a^p$. More straightforwardly, we can set $R^{(1)}=R$ and take the map $R^{(1)}=R\rightarrow R$ to be the Frobenius.} Then: \begin{enumerate} \item The map $\Omega^n_R \otimes_R S \to \Omega^n_S$ is an isomorphism. \item The de Rham differentials $d: \Omega^{n-1}_R \to \Omega^n_R, \Omega^{n-1}_S \to \Omega^n_S$ are respectively $R^{(1)}, S^{(1)}$-linear so that the quotients $\Omega^n_R/d \Omega_R^{n-1} , \Omega^n_S/d \Omega_S^{n-1} $ inherit the structure of $R^{(1)}, S^{(1)}$-modules respectively. The map $\Omega^n_R/d \Omega_R^{n-1} \otimes_{R^{(1)}} S^{(1)} \to \Omega^n_S/d\Omega^{n-1}_S$ is an isomorphism. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Differential forms and their quotients by exact forms are quasi-coherent (over the Frobenius twist) along \'etale maps.
assumptions: Let $R \to S$ be an \'etale map of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras.
Let $R^{(1)} \rightarrow R, S^{(1)} \rightarrow S$ be the Frobenius twists of $R$ and $S$.
conclusions: The map $\Omega^n_R \otimes_R S \to \Omega^n_S$ is an isomorphism.
The map $\Omega^n_R/d \Omega_R^{n-1} \otimes_{R^{(1)}} S^{(1)} \to \Omega^n_S/d\Omega^{n-1}_S$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Proof of quasi-coherence along \'etale maps
nodes.statement: Part (1) is standard. Since $R \to S$ is \'etale, the natural square linking $R^{(1)}, R, S^{(1)}$ and $S$ is cocartesian (cf.~\cite[Tag 0EBS]{stacks-project}), which now implies (2).
nodes.statement_short: Standard for (1); for (2) use that the Frobenius-twist square is cocartesian for \'etale maps.

nodes.name: Structure of $K/p$ and $\TC/p$ for ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras (Geisser--Levine, Geisser--Hesselholt)
assumptions: Let $R$ be an ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra.
for each $n \geq 0$
conclusions: There is a natural map $\pi_n ( K(R)/p) \rightarrow \nu^n(R)$, which is an isomorphism if $R$ is local.
There is a functorial exact sequence $0 \to \widetilde{\nu}^{n+1}(R) \to \pi_n ( \TC(R)/p) \to {\nu}^{n}(R) \to 0$.
If $R$ is local, we have a functorial identification $\pi_n ( \knf(R)/p) \simeq \widetilde{\nu}^{n+2}(R)$.

nodes.statement:

Then the first assertion follows from \cite[Thm.~8.3]{GL}, which shows that on smooth varieties over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the Zariski sheafification of the presheaf $\pi_n(K(\cdot)/p)$ is given by $
u^n$. The exact sequence describing $\pi_n( \TC(R)/p)$ actually follows from \eqref{thisdiag}, though we will give a slightly different proof of the stronger second claim. u^n$ and converging to $\pi_*( \TC/p)$. In the 'etale topology, there is a short exact sequence of sheaves $0 	o

nodes.name: Reduce to essentially finite type and quote Geisser--Levine
nodes.statement: First we note that it suffices to prove this theorem in the case where $R$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{F}_p$, by extending using filtered colimits. Then the first assertion follows from \cite[Thm.~8.3]{GL}, which shows that on smooth varieties over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the Zariski sheafification of the presheaf $\pi_n(K(\cdot)/p)$ is given by $\nu^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Filtered-colimit reduction, then cite Geisser--Levine's sheafification result.

u^n) = \widetilde{
u}^n(R)$, and the 'etale descent spectral sequence thus implies the second claim.
